reviewer: adversarial finder (score not authoritative; see PROMPT-STANDARD "How to review a prompt")

gaps.property: 5 (bounded blast radius) + 2 (falsifiable) — an acceptance item that cannot be met inside the builder's lane
gaps.problem: Criterion 9 requires undo to restore terrain to within 1e-3 m per sample, including a road's cut/fill, but §7 forbids writing world.terrain.heights ("read it to snapshot an undo rectangle; never write it") and the ONLY terrain mutation the spec permits is world.terrain.modify(brush) — a radial raise/lower/flatten/smooth with a 1-r^2(3-2r) falloff. Restoring an arbitrary recorded height rectangle to 1e-3 m with that brush is impossible. I checked the tree: writeHeights/flattenStrip do not exist anywhere (ARCHITECTURE §3 lists them under "terrain owes", and roads_r1 blocker 1 calls flattenStrip "the one you already requested"), and roads itself gets its cut/fill by writing h[i]=v straight into T.heights and then calling T.modify with a zero-strength brush purely to bump version and emit terrain:changed (src/modules/roads/build.js:645-660). So the builder must either (a) copy roads' direct-heights write, which the spec bans, or (b) fail criterion 9. Either outcome burns a round.
gaps.fix: Pick one and write it down. Either: (i) explicitly permit the roads pattern for undo only — "snapshot heights[ix0..ix1, iz0..iz1] into the undo entry; on undo write those values back into world.terrain.heights and then call world.terrain.modify({x:cx,z:cz,radius:r,strength:0,mode:'smooth'}) to bump version and emit terrain:changed, exactly as src/modules/roads/build.js:645-660 does" — and cite that precedent so the critic does not read it as an ownership violation; or (ii) require docs/core-requests/tools.md to ask terrain for setHeights(ix0,iz0,ix1,iz1,Float32Array) -> bool, and restate criterion 9 as a degrade-cleanly item like criterion 19 (counters restore exactly, terrain restore is best-effort until that API lands, reason string exact).

gaps.property: 3 (numeric) — a stated number that, if followed, fails the spec's own criterion 6
gaps.problem: §6 tells the builder to keep overlay materials at "linear colour ≤ 2.0 so they stay under the effects bloom threshold (const thr = lerp(2.6, 2.2, night)/exposure)". At night, environment sets exposure = 2.8 (src/modules/environment/index.js:186, lerp(2.8, dayExp, day) with day=0), so thr = 2.2/2.8 = 0.79 — which is exactly the number the cited critic report gives ("well under bloom threshold 0.79", docs/critic/effects_r1.md:86). The spec's own citation contradicts its own instruction: an unlit toneMapped:false overlay at linear 2.0 sits ~2.5x ABOVE the night threshold and blooms, which is precisely the "glowing ghost at night" failure the paragraph is written to prevent, and it fails criterion 6's "bloom on/off pixel diff ≤ 1/255 mean".
gaps.fix: Replace the number with the night-referred one and show the arithmetic: "overlay materials are toneMapped:false with linear output ≤ 0.70 — at 22:00 environment sets exposure 2.8, so thr = 2.2/2.8 = 0.79 (measured as 0.79 in docs/critic/effects_r1.md:86); at noon exposure ≈ 1.15 gives thr ≈ 2.26, so 0.70 is safe at every hour. A near-white at linear 0.55-0.70 encodes to ~200-240/255 after sRGB, which is the p50 band criterion 6 asks for." Also state that the p50/p99 luminance numbers in criterion 6 are measured in ?showcase=tools, where effects is not loaded and there is no grade pass, while the bloom diff is measured in --showcase all — so the two are not the same pixels.

gaps.property: 5 (bounded blast radius) + 2 (falsifiable) — the anti-argument mechanism itself is unbuildable
gaps.problem: Criteria 6 and 22 both require the ribbonBox/wash-centroid crop to be "printed as {x,y,w,h} in the build report and in the shot's .json sidecar, so builder and critic measure the same pixels and there is nothing to argue about". The sidecar is written entirely by tools/screenshot.mjs with a fixed schema (tools/screenshot.mjs:97-104, 114) and there is no hook for a module to inject a field; BUILDER.md forbids touching tools/. So the one device the spec invents to remove builder/critic disagreement cannot be implemented, and criteria 6, 21 and 22 fall back to hand-cropping — the exact thing they ban.
gaps.fix: Move the declared crop to files the builder may write: "the builder's probe writes shots/tools/r1/crops.json = {shot: {ribbonBox:{x,y,w,h}, washBox:{x,y,w,h}}} for every graded shot, and the same table is repeated in docs/builds/tools_r1.json; the critic re-reads api.stats().ribbonBox from its own probe and must land within ±8 px of the recorded box." Delete the reference to the screenshot sidecar.

gaps.problem: Criterion 1 proves the district was built by the tools using "≥ 3 terrain edits (world.terrain.version ≥ 3)". world.terrain.version is bumped by roads' own conform pass on every rebuild (src/modules/roads/build.js:658-660 calls T.modify after writing heights), so simply staging the road spine in §8 step 2 pushes version well past 3 with zero tool sculpts. The item cannot fail, so it does not test what it claims.
gaps.fix: Count the tool's own actions, not the shared version counter: "a probe reads api.history().entries and finds ≥ 3 entries whose label starts 'terrain:', and the knoll at (150,-120) samples ≥ 14 m above the pre-sculpt height at its centre (baseline recorded in shots/tools/r1/crops.json)". Keep the grep, which is the strong half of this item.

gaps.property: 3 (numeric) — a tolerance band a correct implementation misses by construction
gaps.problem: Criterion 21 requires ghost/disc/ring line widths at 1280x720 to stay "within 0.7-1.4x of their 1080p pixel width". World-space ground geometry at the same vertical FOV scales with viewport height: 720/1080 = 0.667x, just under the 0.7 floor. A builder who does the obvious correct thing (world-space rings and ribbons) fails by 5%; a builder who screen-compensates ring widths passes but then has to decide whether the ribbon — which must be "the exact width of the selected road type" per §3 — is also compensated, which would contradict §3. The spec does not say which classes are screen-compensated.
gaps.fix: Split the item: "chips and disc/ring outline strokes are screen-space sized and stay 24-28 px / 0.7-1.4x of their 1080p pixel width at 720p; the ghost ribbon, guide dashes and ground decals are world-space and are expected to scale with viewport height (0.60-0.72x) — measure them, do not hold them to the 0.7 floor."

gaps.property: 2 (falsifiable) — a probe the showcase makes unrunnable
gaps.problem: Criterion 15 requires that after api.select(null)/cancel()/Escape/commit(), stats().ghostVerts === 0 and phase === 'idle' within one frame. But §8 step 8 pins all six poses simultaneously through a "showcase-only multi-preview mode" that api.select() must not expose. In ?showcase=tools those six previews are live, so ghostVerts is never 0 and the probe fails against a correct build. The spec never names how the probe clears the pinned poses. Criterion 15's second half ("no shot shows a stale ghost from a previous pose except the six deliberately pinned showcase poses") is also unfalsifiable from a PNG — a critic cannot distinguish a stale ghost from a pinned one.
gaps.fix: Name the teardown in the §2 api contract: "_showcasePoses(on:boolean) -> int — showcase/probe only, never reachable from select(); false tears down every pinned pose and returns the count removed", and rewrite criterion 15 as: "probe calls api._showcasePoses(false), then for each of select(null), cancel(), Escape and a successful commit(): stats().ghostVerts === 0 and state().phase === 'idle' on the next frame". Drop the un-gradable second sentence.

gaps.property: 2 (falsifiable) — a measurement with no stated method against a moving target
gaps.problem: Criterion 10 asks that preview cells and already-painted cells behind them sample to the same hue at ΔE ≤ 8. zoning's overlay alpha is animated and fading: mix(0.40, 0.55*pulse, vKind) * uOpacity with pulse = 0.80 + 0.20*sin(...) (src/modules/zoning/overlay.js:130-132), so painted high-density cells composite anywhere in 0.44-0.55 alpha while the preview is pinned at 0.40-0.50, and uOpacity is still ramping in early frames. A composite ΔE between two different alphas over grass can exceed 8 for a perfectly correct build. Criterion 4's "no two chips overlap by more than 10% of their area" has the same problem in a different way: chips are 3D geometry, api.stats().chips returns a count only, and no probe or method for measuring pill overlap is defined.
gaps.fix: For 10, compare against the palette, not the neighbour: "the preview cell's unmultiplied colour equals src/modules/zoning/palette.js exactly (probe reads the material uniform), and a screenshot sample of a preview cell is within ΔE ≤ 12 of a painted cell of the same type/density sampled in the same frame". For 4, add the field the check needs to §2's stats() contract: "chipRects:[{x,y,w,h}] in device pixels" and grade overlap off that array rather than off the PNG.

gaps.property: Role-prompt separation (standard §'Rules for role prompts') — an invariant restated per-module, and BUILDER.md currently teaches the opposite
gaps.problem: The spec explains four times (§2 twice, §7's bolded paragraph, §8 step 6) that ctx.modules.<name> IS the api object and .api? silently no-ops. That is verified correct (registry.js:15 and :36), and hud.js:458/518/531 really are broken by it — but it is a framework-wide fact that belongs in BUILDER.md, which today says the wrong thing: "Guard optional dependencies: ctx.modules.props?.api?.place?.(…)" (BUILDER.md, Engineering rules). A builder reads BUILDER.md first and gets the broken form from the role file; every future module spec will need the same four paragraphs, and they will drift. The same applies to §5's whole-frame-budget carve-out, which contradicts CRITIC.md's global pass gate ("draw calls within the declared budget") and is not specific to tools — props (114 calls/1.47 M tris) and buildings (217/2.03 M) already blow it, and both of the spec's numbers there check out.
gaps.fix: Fix BUILDER.md's guard example to ctx.modules.props?.place?.(…) and add one line to it: "ctx.modules.<name> is the api object; there is no .api indirection (registry.js:15/36)." Add one line to CRITIC.md: "where a module spec says so, the draw-call gate is the module's own group-visibility diff, not the whole frame." Then cut the spec's four paragraphs to a single sentence plus the hud.js:458/518/531 core request, which IS module-specific and should stay.

gaps.property: 2 (falsifiable) — three items that are art-director opinions in checklist clothing
gaps.problem: Criterion 3 ("each is identifiable by its own colour and shape without reading the chips"), criterion 2's second half ("no shimmer, no stripe of asphalt punching through, and no dark seam"), and criterion 17's "a smooth dome — no sheer wall, no rectangular cut" have no observation method, so they will be argued. Counted honestly: about 16 of the 22 items are mechanically checkable end-to-end; 6 have a judgement half.
gaps.fix: Attach the numbers that already exist elsewhere in the spec. For 3: "a probe returns the six poses' screen-space AABBs; none overlaps another by >25% and each pose's dominant hue differs from every other by ≥ 40 degrees". For 2: "the z-fight check is a two-frame pixel diff over the ribbon/asphalt crossing crop with the camera static — mean |diff| ≤ 1/255" (the same on/off diff device criterion 6 already uses). For 17: "probe samples 16 radii out from the sculpt centre; the height profile is monotone and no adjacent 2 m pair differs by more than 1.5 m".

gaps.property: 1 (sequenced) / 9 (resumable) — the shots the criteria name are not the shots the tooling produces
gaps.problem: §4 grades against roadtool_12.png, zonetool_12.png, sculpt_12.png, bulldoze_12.png, invalid_12.png and 6p5/22 variants, but tools/gauntlet.mjs shoots only aerial,street,skyline,closeup by default (tools/gauntlet.mjs:11) — module presets are not included, and §8's "also required before the round is closed" list names only the two --showcase all runs and the 720p pass. The builder can derive it (CRITIC.md tells the critic to shoot declared presets), but the round can close with half the graded shots missing.
gaps.fix: Add the exact command to §8: "node tools/gauntlet.mjs --module tools --round <r> --cameras roadtool,zonetool,sculpt,bulldoze,service,invalid --times 12,22 (plus 6.5 for roadtool)" alongside the existing required runs.

strengths: Every factual claim I could check is true. I verified: registry.js:15/36 (ctx.modules = this.apis), hud.js:458/518/531 (the .api? indirection bug is real, and the eight tool: strings in buildCategories exactly match ACCEPTED), showcase.js:22-30, effects/index.js:141 (the thr formula verbatim), terrain/water.js:192 (reflCam.layers.disable(LAYERS.HELPERS)), zoning/grid.js:458-468 (install() surface, and world.zones.bulk genuinely does not exist), zoning/index.js:54 and :92-118, zoning/palette.js (all eight hex values verbatim), buildings/index.js:233-251, simulation/index.js:196-206, props/index.js:234-249 (api is exactly {rebuild,stats,lamps,signalState,count,serialize,deserialize} and there is no place()), world.js:73-77 and :94-103, the three stubs at services/transit/infoviews index.js:9, roads/network.js:288-296, terrain/index.js:40-57, constants (LAYERS.HELPERS 8, RENDER_ORDER 100/200, TILE_SIZE 128, BUDGET.perModuleDrawCalls.tools 20), camera.registerPreset and the real closeup/street/aerial/skyline preset values, events.listenerCount, and __sim.stats().moduleMs. Zero invented APIs — rare and worth saying.

The cited failure modes are all real and correctly attributed. effects_r1.md:49 does contain "bloom on/off diff 0.00 (nothing crosses threshold 2.26)" and :86 is the night/lamp-head blocker; roads_r1 blockers 1 and 3 and issue 6 ("rectangular dark cut in the knoll") are as described; terrain_r1 blocker 1 is grass in the planar reflection; environment_r1 blocker 3 and simulation_r1 issue 1 are both the 13 m lattice; ui_r1 issues 1-2 are the RCI overflow and the 720p break; environment_r2's "milky and blown" at 17:30 is quoted correctly. §6 is project memory, not generic advice.

The reference reading is accurate. I looked at $REF/cs2_1.jpg: it is the road tool mid-drag over a roundabout, and every element the spec enumerates is there and correctly characterised — opaque paint-like white ribbon, dashed white guide beyond the cursor, flat white node discs with a pale cyan halo on the live node, saturated blue wash over the island with a brighter edge and trees visible through it, dark rounded pills with leading glyphs reading exactly 39 m / 14 deg / 61 m / -7.7 % / 85 deg / 41 m, and a green-glyph c616 chip pinned to the cursor node. The instruction to reproduce the world-space overlay and not the HUD, and to not declare ui as a dependency, is the right call.

Criterion 19 is the best-written item in any spec in this repo: it distinguishes two different reasons a neighbour cannot place (props is finished but has no place(); services is a stub whose world.services.place returns null), gates on typeof ctx.modules.props?.place === 'function' rather than a version flag, fixes both reason strings exactly, and requires the ghost to still render with zero console errors and status ready. That is a criterion a critic can grade in one probe and a builder cannot argue with.

The anchors in §3 are genuinely worked at each point (10/9/8.5/7/5/3), module-specific, and each names what an observer would look at — the 9 and 8.5 anchors in particular give a critic a real discriminator (chip typography vs everything else).

The budget section is honest about what it cannot control: the whole-frame figure is explicitly recorded-not-graded, backed by the real measured numbers from shots/props/dev_aerial_12.json (1 473 859 tris / 114 calls) and shots/buildings/rdev1/summary.json (maxTriangles 2 034 862, maxDrawCalls 217), which I confirmed, plus a standing instruction to name which module owns any excess rather than thinning the district. The declared-vs-measured split (20/40 000 ceiling, 12/20 000 target) is stated identically in §5 and criterion 13.
§8 closes with its assumptions stated rather than asked (the whole cost table, grade limits) and requires them in one exported table the critic can read — property 7 done properly.
verdict: 8.0 — fails at 8.5, but only just, and for four concrete reasons rather than vagueness. This is the most rigorously verified module spec in the repo: I checked every named API, line reference, critic citation and measured number against the code and the shot JSONs, and all of them are correct, including the hud.js .api bug, the props-has-no-place finding, and the eight-string ACCEPTED list. Two competent builders would produce very nearly the same module from this text — which is exactly why it is worth failing on the places where they would not. Lens 1: the builder must guess how to restore terrain on undo (criterion 9 demands 1e-3 m restoration while §7 bans writing heights and the only permitted brush cannot do it — roads gets away with it by writing h[i] directly at build.js:645-660, which is the precedent the spec should either grant or replace with a core request); must guess the night brightness ceiling (the stated \"linear ≤ 2.0\" is ~2.5x above the 0.79 night threshold that the spec's own cited critic line measured, and following it produces the glowing ghost §6 exists to prevent); and cannot implement the declared-crop mechanism at all, because the .json sidecar is written by tools/screenshot.mjs which the builder may not touch. Lens 2: about 16 of 22 items grade cleanly on a probe or a named pixel measurement — high — but criterion 15's ghostVerts probe cannot run against the six pinned showcase poses, criterion 1's terrain.version proxy passes vacuously because roads bumps it, criterion 10's ΔE ≤ 8 fights zoning's animated overlay alpha, criterion 21's 0.7x floor excludes the 0.667x that correct world-space geometry produces at 720p, and criteria 3/17 leave a judgement half. Each of those is one round or one argument. Fix the four ranked gaps and the framework-invariant duplication (BUILDER.md still teaches the broken ctx.modules.props?.api?.place?.() form, and CRITIC.md's global draw-call gate needs the group-diff carve-out that is not specific to tools) and this is a 9.
